questions.q: Who officially became the head of India after the Government of India Act of 1858?
questions.a: Queen Victoria became the Empress of India. A wrong answer suggests the student is still confusing the "East India Company" with the "British Government," showing they missed the fundamental shift in who held authority.

questions.q: Why did the British government appoint a Viceroy in India after 1858?
questions.a: The Viceroy was appointed as the direct representative of the British Crown to oversee the governance of India. A wrong answer suggests the student thinks the Viceroy was an elected leader, which misses the point that this was an appointed position for colonial control.

questions.q: If you were a British official in 1860, why would you recruit more soldiers from groups categorized as "martial races"?
questions.a: You would do this to create a more loyal and effective army that would be less likely to join another revolt against the British. A wrong answer suggests the student does not understand that army reforms were a strategy to maintain security and prevent future uprisings.

questions.q: How did the British approach to taking over new Indian kingdoms change after 1858?
questions.a: They became much more cautious about annexing (taking over) new territories to avoid upsetting local rulers and causing more unrest. A wrong answer suggests the student hasn't grasped that the British were trying to stabilize their rule rather than just expanding rapidly.

questions.q: Was the transition to Crown Rule more about improving life for Indians or securing British control?
questions.a: It was primarily about securing British control to prevent another revolt like 1857. A wrong answer shows the student is failing to see the "why" behind political changes, often mistakenly assuming all government reforms are purely for public welfare.

questions.q: If you were a Viceroy in 1865, what two changes would you tell your staff to make to ensure the British rule stays strong?
questions.a: A good answer includes: 1) Increasing the number of British soldiers in the army to outnumber Indian soldiers, and 2) Recruiting from specific groups they felt were loyal. A poor answer focuses on irrelevant things like trade or taxes, showing the student hasn't connected the army changes to the goal of preventing revolts.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Crown Rule (or the British Raj) was the period starting in 1858 when the British ______ took direct control of India, ending the rule of the East India Company.
Fill in the blank: Imagine if your school was run by a ______ club that suddenly caused a huge argument among the students, leading the Education Board to step in and take direct charge.
Fill in the blank: Crown Rule (or the British Raj) was the period starting in ______ when the British government took direct control of India, ending the rule of the East India Company.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to identify that power shifted from a private company to the British government and explain the change in leadership structure (Viceroy).
